title: Responsive component density, a11y hitbox and scroll quirk triage
creator: Lina Korhonen
description: Full QA sweep focused on density and interactive hit areas for compact components (buttons, table rows, compact charts) across Safari iOS, Safari macOS, Firefox, and Android Chrome. Goal: catalog reproducible visual and interaction regressions introduced by token density changes and the new sticky header implementation; produce prioritized bug triage with recommended fixes and owners.
affected_components: Table: compact rows, sticky header, cell truncation
Chart: compact legend wrapping on narrow viewports
bug_items: BUG-82451-1: Safari iOS (17.x) momentum scroll causes sticky table header to jump on fast swipe. Severity: high. Repro: open compact table on iPhone 15 Pro, fast flick down then up, header detaches then reattaches with 1-3px vertical offset. Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/safari-ios-header-jump.png. Suggested fix: transition to transform-based sticky header (translateY) and avoid forced layout on scroll handlers; coordinate with ENG-41220 runtime repaint mitigation. Owner: ENG - Evan Martinez. Status: Investigating

BUG-82451-2: Firefox Desktop (stable) ellipsis truncation drops last character in some languages (German umlauts) when density token set to compact-2. Severity: medium. Repro: narrow window to 720px and inspect table cell with single-line truncation. Root cause hypothesis: subpixel rounding plus font fallback. Suggested fix: fallback letter-spacing or clip-path tweak; design suggests adding 2px right padding in compact mode for FF only. Owner: DES - Priya Sharma. Status: Proposed fix

BUG-82451-3: Android Chrome (Samsung) touch targets for compact toolbar buttons under 40px visual size fail a11y touch target heuristic. Severity: high (a11y). Repro: open app shell in mobile webview, attempt to tap small icon buttons in compact mode. Suggested fix: increase hitbox via padding or pointer-event hit-area pseudo-element while keeping visual size. Owner: ENG - Mateo Alvarez. Status: In Progress

BUG-82451-4: macOS Safari form controls in dense tables lose focus ring when using keyboard navigation after a scroll that triggered sticky header. Severity: P2 (usability). Repro: tab through table after scrolling. Suggested fix: ensure focus styling is applied to focus-visible and re-evaluate z-index/gpu-layering. Owner: DES - Lina Korhonen + ENG - Casey Wu. Status: Needs design review

BUG-82451-5: Chart legend wraps inconsistently on mobile - causes layout jump on orientation change in compact density. Severity: low. Repro: rotate device from portrait to landscape. Suggested fix: use flex-wrap with min-width clamp and reserve line height in compact tokens. Owner: DES - Marco Li. Status: Backlog
reproduction_notes: Primary repro devices: iPhone 15 Pro iOS 17.2 Safari, macOS Ventura Safari stable, Firefox 125 beta/125 stable, Pixel 7 Android 14 Chrome. Also test within Electron-based app shell used by customers.
Use the 'compact-2' token set via the demo page query param ?density=compact-2 to reproduce density-specific issues. Toggle RTL for truncation edgecases.
Enable reduced-motion to verify sticky header transition fallbacks.
Record with iOS Screen Recording and attach the mp4 to the ticket for scroll-jump bugs.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: prefer increasing hit target via invisible padding over increasing visual component size to preserve compact layout; trade-off: slightly more complex CSS and potential layout noise in some browsers.
Decision: implement transform-based sticky header to reduce layout thrashing; trade-off: need to manage stacking context and z-index for dropdowns anchored to table cells.
Trade-off: Firefox-specific 2px right padding for truncation vs. global padding change. We prefer browser-specific tweak to avoid affecting macOS Safari rendering.
attachments: Related ENG work: ENG-41220 (runtime repaint mitigation), ENG-42811 (touch-hitbox util)
next_steps: (Design) Finalize recommended hitbox CSS snippet and verify with accessibility team by 2025-03-07. Owner: Priya Sharma.
(Engineering) Spike implement transform-based sticky header in a feature branch and run cross-browser perf profile. Owner: Evan Martinez. ETA: 2025-03-10.
Create a small e2e test harness that runs on BrowserStack for iOS Safari and Firefox desktop for the three highest-severity repros. Owner: QA - Rosa Kim. ETA: 2025-03-12.
Ship quick-fix patch for Firefox truncation if engineering spike confirms 2px padding resolves without regressions. Owner: Mateo Alvarez. ETA: 2025-03-14.
Add automated visual regression thresholds for compact density tokens in Percy snapshots. Owner: Design Ops - Marco Li. ETA: 2025-03-20.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Lina Korhonen: Initial triage completed. Collected 6 video repros from product QA. Prioritizing Safari iOS header jump and Android touch targets.

2025-02-25 - Evan Martinez: Spike started to reproduce header jump. Preliminary finding: scroll handlers in table container trigger layout reflow due to read-before-write pattern. Trying transform approach.
2025-02-27 - Priya Sharma: Design propose CSS utility .hit-area-expand and a spec for 44x44 effective hit targets while keeping 32px visuals. Attached Figma examples.
2025-03-01 - Rosa Kim: BrowserStack run added to QA pipeline; initial runs show flaky pass on iOS 16 devices. Will rerun on 3 consecutive runs to confirm.
2025-03-04 - Casey Wu: Eng notes - transform sticky resolved one reproduction case but introduced z-index clipping for dropdowns anchored to table cells. Adding follow-up task ENG-42812.
notes_for_release_notes: Addresses compact-density interaction regressions across Safari and Firefox; improves mobile touch target a11y for compact controls. Backported patch may be needed for customers using older webviews.
